first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous declines in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ), with competitive pressure on price-sensitive SMBs. Verifying memory_86 and memory_91 tests whether the durable gains from shortening onboarding and activation messaging remain valid. Activation messaging is the primary candidate because: (1) it directly addresses the 6% activation decline without the retention risks flagged in memory_73 around promotional pricing; (2) it complements onboarding improvements rather than substituting them; (3) it works with established product flow rather than requiring pricing structure changes that could harm enterprise positioning; (4) referral incentives (memory_57) require healthy existing retention to work, which is currently declining. Promotional pricing is explicitly ruled out due to memory_73's clear warning about retention harm. A standard_experiment on activation_messaging preserves the ability to layer in onboarding refinements or enterprise sales assist in future weeks while maintaining focus on qualified revenue sustainability. The enterprise_sales_assist direction is secondary but not primary because it addresses a different segment than the immediate competitive threat.
